projects.title: Sunny's Bookshop
projects.lede: An independent bookshop with a brand its readers already loved needed it ready for a second store. The book was redrawn by hand; the rest was put in order.

image.alt: The Sunny’s Bookshop seal in vellum on Library Green.

projects.title: 22nd Anniversary | Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival
projects.lede: For its 22nd edition, HollyShorts got a poster painted by hand: the festival itself, from the red carpet to the screen. Its dancing figures then walked onto every badge, sign and bottle.

image.alt: The 2026 HollyShorts poster, a hand painting of the festival.

projects.title: Opmet Serif
projects.lede: Opmet Serif, the typeface of Opmet Osserpse: how it started from the founder’s handwriting, its wink, how its letters are drawn and the whole font.

image.alt: Two facing book pages set in Opmet Serif: a chapter opening in Display Italic, with justified text in Text Regular, small caps and a pull quote in italic.

projects.title: 10th Anniversary | HollyShorts Comedy Film Festival
projects.lede: For its 10th anniversary the comedy festival got a poster built like a set: a clapperboard, a director's chair, a rubber duck and banana peels on hot pink. Then it started to move.

image.alt: The 10th anniversary HollyShorts Comedy poster: comedy props on hot pink.

projects.title: Solebury Home Watch Services
projects.lede: A home watch service looks after houses while their owners are away. Its new mark says so in one image: an owl keeping watch from the roof.

image.alt: The Solebury Home Watch Services logo: an owl on the roof of a house, in white on blue.

projects.title: Polish Film Festival North America
projects.lede: A Polish film festival held in Los Angeles got a poster that belongs to both cities' traditions, painted after rounds of red-marker studies.

image.alt: The Polish Film Festival North America poster.

projects.title: Weissman 2025/2026 Catalog
projects.lede: The Weissman 2025/2026 Catalog runs to 136 pages and six themed sections. Its layouts began on set, beside the shoot, over 14 days in Los Angeles.

image.alt: The cover of the Weissman 2025/2026 Catalog.

projects.title: 21st Anniversary | Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival
projects.lede: The 21st anniversary poster began on an easel, in pencil, then moved through a sketchbook of color studies. From there it spread to badges, merchandise, a metal award and three events.

image.alt: The 21st anniversary HollyShorts poster.

projects.title: Red Mask
projects.lede: To build the world of an independent feature, Ritesh Films commissioned the one-sheets of a horror franchise that never was: 13 films over 25 years, each poster true to its year.

image.alt: “Red Mask: Night of Blood,” the first poster in the series.

projects.title: Inaugural Edition | HollyShorts Dubai
projects.lede: The first HollyShorts in Dubai needed a whole identity at once. It came from one image, the Burj Khalifa in watercolor under a pink and blue sky.

image.alt: The HollyShorts Dubai 2025 poster: the Burj Khalifa in watercolor.

projects.title: Don't Let Them Out
projects.client: “Don't Let Them Out,” directed by Lila McLaughlin
projects.lede: For Lila McLaughlin's short film, the poster went from a page of thumbnail sketches to two finals, then off the screen and onto paper and tees.

image.alt: The “Don’t Let Them Out” poster.

projects.title: Second Edition | BAFTA®-Qualifying HollyShorts London
projects.lede: A second year in London meant growing the identity without starting over. The 2025 system carried from the poster to the jury, the schedule and the award show screen.

image.alt: The HollyShorts London 2025 poster.

projects.title: Ninth Anniversary | HollyShorts Comedy Film Festival
projects.lede: After three years designing the Hollywood Comedy Shorts Film Festival, Opmet Osserpse led its rebrand into HollyShorts Comedy: a new name, closer to the parent festival, with the jokes left in.

image.alt: The 2025 HollyShorts Comedy poster.

projects.title: Key art and pitch decks for Tremor House
Inaugural Edition | BAFTA®-Qualifying HollyShorts London
projects.lede: When HollyShorts first came to London, its identity started as pencil drawings of the clock tower. On the poster a film strip winds round it; on the badges, small drawn figures mark each pass.

image.alt: The HollyShorts London 2024 poster: Big Ben with a film strip.

projects.title: 20th Anniversary | Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival
projects.lede: For its 20th anniversary, HollyShorts got an original illustration of the Chinese Theatre. It went on a poster, a photo wall drawn first as a sketch, 10 badges and a full merchandise line.

image.alt: The 20th anniversary HollyShorts poster.

projects.title: Cannes 2024
projects.lede: A year after the HollyShorts invitation, Kodak's events at Cannes got the same fine blue line: the town's streets and buildings, drawn for posters and invitations.

image.alt: A blue line drawing of a Cannes street.

projects.title: Skyfire Artists
projects.lede: For Skyfire Artists, a single mark, a lightning bolt breaking out of a square, carries everything from the wall sign and business card to the merch. In motion, it splits into color.

image.alt: The Skyfire Artists logo on a wall sign.

projects.title: Survived By
projects.lede: For K.D. Chalk's “Survived By,” the one-sheet is a single illustrated figure: a woman in pink, holding a record.

image.alt: The “Survived By” one-sheet.

projects.title: “LiTTLE iSSUES”
projects.client: “LiTTLE iSSUES,” created by Jana Miley and directed by Jerah Milligan
projects.lede: “LiTTLE iSSUES,” created by Jana Miley and directed by Jerah Milligan, is a short film that has won over a dozen awards. Its poster looks in on three people in a warm, dim living room, under the title in round yellow letters.

image.alt: The “LiTTLE iSSUES” poster.

projects.title: Branding and packaging for Kimberla Lawson Roby
Book design for a private client
Cannes 2023
projects.lede: For HollyShorts' events at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival, the invitation was a drawing: the coast in a fine blue line, and above the details, “Tu es invité.”

image.alt: The 2023 Cannes invitation: a blue line drawing above “Tu es invité.”

projects.title: Miles Regis
projects.lede: Miles Regis paints crowds of figures and words. For his coloring book, each painting was redrawn by hand as a black line, leaving the color to the reader.

image.alt: A line drawing adapted from a Miles Regis painting.

projects.title: 19th Anniversary | Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival
projects.lede: In 2023, Opmet Osserpse became the festival's art director. The edition's painted palms, sea and red carpet went onto Hollywood billboards and badges, and onto a list of the world's best festival posters.

image.alt: The 2023 HollyShorts poster.

projects.title: “Nice Knives”
projects.lede: “Nice Knives” is a short film directed by Connor Copeland and distributed by BAM In Motion. Its poster is a still life: a ham on a cutting board with bread, cheese and butter, a knife standing upright, under the title in bright yellow.

image.alt: The “Nice Knives” poster.

projects.title: “Let This Feeling Go”
projects.client: “Let This Feeling Go,” directed by Andrew De Zen
projects.lede: “Let This Feeling Go” was directed by Andrew De Zen in Los Angeles. Its original artwork and poster paint a woman in thick strokes, in two versions, one yellow and white, one red, the title in hand lettering beside her face.

image.alt: The “Let This Feeling Go” poster, in yellow and white.

projects.title: 18th Anniversary | Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival
projects.lede: The first of five HollyShorts editions. In 2022, as a designer, Opmet Osserpse made the festival's graphics and social media, from the official selection laurel to the podcast.

image.alt: The 2022 official selection laurel.

projects.title: “Welcome Home”
projects.lede: “Welcome Home” is a short film written and directed by Jo Rochelle. Its poster paints two people sitting on the grass, their backs to us, facing a white house under palm trees and a blue sky, in two versions.

image.alt: The “Welcome Home” poster.

projects.title: Production artist for a feature film
HDtracks
projects.lede: HDtracks sells high-resolution music to people who care how a recording sounds. In 2019 the store was rebranded and rebuilt from the ground up, from the database to the logo, so a deep catalog reads as clearly as it sounds. Around it runs a year-round line of campaigns and email. Retention and sales rose.

image.alt: The HDtracks store: charts in the sidebar, featured collections and the newest high-resolution albums.

projects.title: Chop Suey Club
projects.lede: Chop Suey Club is a contemporary gallery and design boutique in Manhattan, focused on Chinese artists. We were a founding member of the studio, responsible for design, social media, content strategy, sponsorships and live events.

image.alt: A plain red square.
